$comment: Whole looks. Each style sets style tokens (tokens/styles/styles.css) and recommends a palette, type pairing and corner radius that suit it.

styles.name: Studio
styles.summary: Hairline borders, soft surfaces, one accent and almost no shadow. The calm default for products people use all day.
styles.useFor: Dashboards, settings, admin tools, most SaaS products.
styles.notTo: Minimal, which removes the borders and most of the chrome as well.
styles.brief: Keep chrome quiet so content leads.

styles.name: Swiss
styles.summary: Square corners, strong black rules, a tight grid and one signal red. Type does the work, decoration does none.
styles.useFor: Agencies, portfolios, conference sites, editorial product pages.
styles.notTo: Brutalism, which also drops decoration but keeps browser-default parts and ignores the grid.
styles.brief: Align everything to a strict grid and let type size carry hierarchy.

styles.name: Editorial
styles.summary: Serif display type, thin rules instead of boxes, generous margins. Reads like a well-set magazine.
signals: wide margins and a narrow measure
styles.useFor: Publications, essays, portfolios, research and annual reports.
styles.notTo: Newsprint, which is denser, uses double rules and packs more columns.
styles.brief: Separate with rules and space, not cards.

styles.name: Neobrutalism
aliases: bright blocks with black outlines and hard shadows
styles.summary: Thick ink outlines, hard offset shadows with zero blur, flat saturated blocks. Buttons physically press down.
styles.useFor: Creator tools, playful consumer apps, launches that want to be remembered.
styles.notTo: Brutalism, which uses raw browser defaults and no colour at all.
styles.brief: Every surface gets an ink outline and a solid offset shadow; pressing a button removes its shadow.

styles.name: Terminal
styles.summary: Monospace everywhere, dashed rules, square corners and a phosphor accent on near-black.
styles.useFor: CLIs, developer tools, infra status pages, changelogs.
styles.notTo: Blueprint, which is technical too but uses a drawn grid and blue lines.
styles.brief: Treat the screen like a console: mono type, dashed separators, no rounded corners.

styles.name: Glass
aliases: frosted cards over a soft background
styles.summary: Translucent, blurred panels over a soft single-hue glow, with a thin light edge. Calm, not rainbow.
signals: thin light edge on every panel
styles.useFor: Media apps, dashboards over imagery, consumer widgets.
styles.notTo: The purple-to-pink gradient hero, which this deliberately avoids.
styles.brief: Panels are 70% opaque with a 16px backdrop blur over a quiet glow; keep text contrast checked.

styles.name: Soft UI
aliases: soft buttons pushed out of the background
styles.summary: Surfaces share the page colour and lift out of it with paired light and dark shadows. Fields press in.
signals: surfaces the same colour as the page
borders kept on inputs for contrast
styles.useFor: Calm consumer apps, smart-home and wellness controls.
styles.notTo: Clay, which is puffier, more colourful and uses inner highlights.
styles.brief: Raise cards with soft paired shadows; keep a visible border on every input.

styles.name: Clay
styles.summary: Puffy rounded objects with an inner highlight, an inner shade and a soft drop, like modelling clay.
styles.useFor: Kids, habits, games, playful onboarding.
styles.notTo: Soft UI, which stays the page colour and avoids inner highlights.
styles.brief: Round everything generously and give surfaces an inner highlight and a soft drop.

styles.name: Classic Desktop
styles.summary: Bevelled buttons, inset fields and square windows from 1990s desktop software, kept crisp.
styles.useFor: Nostalgic products, games, utilities, playful internal tools.
styles.notTo: Skeuomorphism, which imitates real materials rather than old software.
styles.brief: Buttons get a light top-left and dark bottom-right bevel; fields are inset.

styles.name: Blueprint
styles.summary: A faint drawn grid behind everything, dashed construction lines and mono labels. Looks measured.
styles.useFor: Hardware, infrastructure, API references, architecture diagrams.
styles.notTo: Terminal, which has no grid and is all text.
styles.brief: Put a 24px grid behind the page and draw separators as dashed lines.

styles.name: Lucid Dark
styles.summary: Near-black panels with a faint top highlight and a 1px inner edge. Dense, quiet and precise.
styles.useFor: Developer tools, issue trackers, pro dashboards.
styles.notTo: Glass, which is translucent and blurred.
styles.brief: Give panels a 1px inner edge and a faint top-to-bottom sheen; keep everything compact.

styles.name: Flat
aliases: everything is just solid colors with no shadows
styles.summary: Solid fills, no borders on surfaces, no shadows, no gradients. Hierarchy comes from colour blocks.
styles.useFor: Public services, kiosks, simple consumer apps.
styles.notTo: Minimal, which keeps borders thin and uses mostly white space.
styles.brief: Remove borders and shadows from surfaces and separate areas with fills.

styles.name: Minimal
aliases: the page with almost nothing on it
styles.summary: Very few elements, wide spacing, underline fields and text-like buttons. Empty space is the material.
styles.useFor: Luxury, architecture, fashion, single-product sites.
styles.notTo: Flat, which fills areas with solid colour blocks.
styles.brief: Cut every element that is not essential and double the spacing between what remains.

sample.title: Fewer, better
sample.body: Oak · made to last thirty years

styles.name: Paper
styles.summary: A faint paper grain, warm ink and pressed-in labels. Tactile without imitating leather or wood.
styles.useFor: Invitations, journals, stationery, recipe and hospitality sites.
styles.notTo: Skeuomorphism, which copies specific real objects in detail.
styles.brief: Add a very faint grain to the page and a soft paper drop to cards.

styles.name: Elevated
styles.summary: Borderless cards lifted by layered soft shadows, rounded corners and plenty of room.
styles.useFor: Consumer apps, mobile-first products, marketplaces.
styles.notTo: Soft UI, where surfaces share the page colour.
styles.brief: Drop borders on cards and lift them with a two-layer shadow.

styles.name: Newsprint
styles.summary: Dense serif text, double rules, tight columns and almost no colour. Information first.
styles.useFor: News, data journalism, archives, long dense reference pages.
styles.notTo: Editorial, which is airier and uses single thin rules.
styles.brief: Set dense serif columns divided by double rules; use colour only for alerts.

styles.name: Monochrome
styles.summary: Black, white and greys only. The accent becomes ink, so hierarchy comes from weight, size and space.
styles.useFor: Developer tools, documentation, portfolios, anything that should feel quiet and exact.
styles.notTo: Minimal, which keeps a brand colour; monochrome removes it entirely.
styles.brief: Set the accent to ink and let typography carry every decision.

styles.name: Graphite
styles.summary: Near-black surfaces, crisp hairlines, small corners and mono labels. No glow, no gradients.
signals: near-black canvas with one step lighter cards
styles.useFor: Developer tools, infrastructure dashboards, trading and monitoring screens.
styles.notTo: Terminal, which goes green-on-black and fully mono; graphite keeps a sans body.
styles.brief: Draw structure with hairlines and spacing; keep colour for state.

styles.name: Atelier
styles.summary: High-contrast serif headings, wide margins, thin rules and almost no boxes. Feels printed.
styles.useFor: Brands, studios, hospitality, galleries, premium product launches.
styles.notTo: Editorial, which is denser and reads like a magazine; atelier is sparse like a gallery wall.
styles.brief: Give every element twice the space you think it needs and remove one border.

styles.name: Nordic
styles.summary: Warm greys, rounded shapes, filled surfaces instead of borders and gentle low shadows.
styles.useFor: Health, wellbeing, home and family apps, onboarding flows, consumer tools.
styles.notTo: Soft, which uses pastel tints and puffier shadows; nordic stays grey and restrained.
styles.brief: Swap borders for filled surfaces and keep every shadow below 8px blur.

styles.name: Kraft
styles.summary: Warm paper ground, slab-serif headings, dashed rules and a terracotta accent. Feels hand-made but stays tidy.
styles.useFor: Food and drink, independent shops, studios, newsletters, community sites.
styles.notTo: Retro, which leans on chunky offset shadows and pastel; kraft is quieter and warmer.
styles.brief: Use the paper ground and slab headings; let dashed rules do the dividing.

styles.name: Midnight
styles.summary: Deep navy surfaces, soft corners and a warm sand accent. Darker and calmer than plain dark mode.
styles.useFor: Finance, wellness at night, media apps, premium consumer products.
styles.notTo: Glass, which blurs and glows; midnight stays solid.
styles.brief: Keep the ground deep and the accent warm; never pure black.

styles.name: Playful
styles.summary: Big rounded corners, chunky buttons that press down, rounded type and a bright accent.
signals: buttons with a bottom edge that presses
styles.useFor: Education, kids and family, games-adjacent apps, onboarding.
styles.notTo: Neobrutalism, which uses black outlines; playful uses soft colour edges.
styles.brief: Make every control a little bigger and give buttons a pressable bottom edge.

styles.name: Enterprise
styles.summary: Dense but calm: grey canvas, white cards with fine borders, compact controls and no decoration.
styles.useFor: Admin consoles, CRMs, HR and finance tools, internal software.
styles.notTo: Studio, which is airier; enterprise packs more onto the screen without crowding it.
styles.brief: Set density to dense and let borders, not colour, separate things.

styles.name: Zen
styles.summary: Almost nothing: wide margins, light weights, no borders and one muted accent used once.
styles.useFor: Journaling, meditation, reading apps, personal sites.
styles.notTo: Minimal, which keeps borders and normal weights; zen removes both.
styles.brief: Remove every border, lighten the type and give the one action room.

styles.name: Tonal
styles.summary: Surfaces tinted with the accent instead of grey, pill buttons, big corners and no borders.
signals: secondary buttons filled with a tint
styles.useFor: Mobile-first apps, Android-leaning products, friendly consumer tools.
styles.notTo: Nordic, which uses neutral grey fills; tonal tints everything with the accent.
styles.brief: Tint every surface slightly with the accent and make buttons pills.

styles.name: System
styles.summary: Grouped, inset lists on a grey ground, translucent bars, quiet separators and bold large titles.
signals: white inset groups with rounded corners
hairline separators inset from the left
styles.useFor: Settings screens, mobile web apps, companion apps for native products.
styles.notTo: Enterprise, which is denser and squarer; system follows phone conventions.
styles.brief: Group related rows into rounded white blocks on a grey ground.

styles.name: Noir
styles.summary: Near-black, white serif headlines and no colour at all. Dramatic, quiet and expensive.
styles.useFor: Fashion, film, hospitality, galleries, launch pages for premium products.
styles.notTo: Graphite, which is a working tool UI; noir is for brands and stories.
styles.brief: Remove colour, keep contrast, and let a serif carry the drama.

styles.name: Bauhaus
styles.summary: Geometric type, thick ink rules, square blocks and one red circle as the signature.
styles.useFor: Design studios, architecture, museums, events, bold portfolios.
styles.notTo: Swiss, which relies on grid and grotesk type; bauhaus adds geometric marks.
styles.brief: Draw structure with 2px ink lines and mark labels with a red circle.

styles.name: Ticker
styles.summary: Black, amber accents, mono numbers, tight rows and hairline grids. Built for screens full of data.
styles.useFor: Trading, monitoring, operations rooms, analytics power users.
styles.notTo: Terminal, which is green and text-first; ticker is for tables and numbers.
styles.brief: Set density to dense and use mono for every number.

styles.name: Linen
styles.summary: Warm off-white, a bookish serif, an oxblood accent and soft corners. Calm and well-read.
styles.useFor: Publishers, writing tools, education, considered consumer brands.
styles.notTo: Paper, which adds a texture and print shadows; linen stays smooth.
styles.brief: Raise the line height, use the serif for headings, and keep the accent for links.

styles.name: Signal
styles.summary: Large tight headlines, a saturated cobalt for every action and square, heavy buttons.
styles.useFor: Developer platforms, fintech, product launches that need to feel decisive.
styles.notTo: Neobrutalism, which uses black outlines and offsets; signal stays clean.
styles.brief: Make headlines bigger and tighter and give every action the cobalt.
